## Mathematical Review

# Critic Analysis — rm-01271 (Partition hook-length identities)

## Problem restatement
For $\lambda\vdash n$ with cells $u$ of hook length $h_u$, fix $\alpha\in\mathbb C$ and formal $q$. Decide as identities of formal power series in $x$:
(i) Hook-length: $\sum_{n\ge1}x^n\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\sum_{u\in\lambda}q^{h_u^\alpha}=P(x)\sum_{k\ge1}q^{k^\alpha}\frac{x^k}{1-x^k}$.
(ii) Parts: $\sum_{n\ge1}x^n\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\sum_i q^{\lambda_i^\alpha}=P(x)\sum_{k\ge1}q^{k^\alpha}\frac{x^k}{1-x^k}$, with $P(x)=\prod_k(1-x^k)^{-1}$.
Treat $Q_k:=q^{k^\alpha}$ as independent indeterminates.

## Verdict (numerically verified, n<=12): (ii) is TRUE, (i) is FALSE.

## Background
$P(x)=\sum_n p(n)x^n$ (Euler). Parts statistic: $\sum_i q^{\lambda_i^\alpha}=\sum_k \mathrm{mult}_k(\lambda)Q_k$. Hook statistic: $\sum_u q^{h_u^\alpha}=\sum_v H_v(\lambda)Q_v$, $H_v=\#\{u:h_u=v\}$. Classical fact: $N_k(n)=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\mathrm{mult}_k(\lambda)=\sum_{m\ge1}p(n-km)$, i.e. $\sum_n N_k(n)x^n=P(x)\frac{x^k}{1-x^k}$ (Andrews). Hook-length distribution differs (Bacher-Manivel, Han).

## Reduction of RHS
$\frac{x^k}{1-x^k}=\sum_{m\ge1}x^{km}$ gives $[x^n]\mathrm{RHS}=\sum_k Q_k R_k(n)$, $R_k(n):=\sum_{m\ge1}p(n-km)$.

## Proof structure
(ii) TRUE: Lemma A $[x^n]\mathrm{LHS(ii)}=\sum_k N_k(n)Q_k$; Lemma B $N_k(n)=\sum_m p(n-km)$ (delete $m$ copies of $k$ bijection); conclude per-$Q_k$ match.
(i) FALSE: Lemma C $[x^n]\mathrm{LHS(i)}=\sum_v M_v(n)Q_v$, $M_v(n)=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}H_v(\lambda)$. Counterexample $n=2$: $(2)$ hooks $\{2,1\}$, $(1,1)$ hooks $\{2,1\}$, so $M_2(2)=2$ but $R_2(2)=p(0)=1$. Coefficient of $Q_2x^2$ is 2 vs 1, so (i) fails.

## Gap analysis (no solution.tex yet; these are the sub-lemmas a solver must establish)
- G1 (rm-01271-2): prove $N_k(n)=\sum_m p(n-km)$ — heart of (ii).
- G2 (rm-01271-3): justify coefficient extraction in independent symbols $Q_k=q^{k^\alpha}$; equality of series <=> per-monomial $Q_k x^n$ equality. Needed to make disproof of (i) airtight.
- G3 (rm-01271-4): establish Lemma C and the explicit $n=2$ counterexample, $\alpha$-independent.

## Difficulty
G1 low-moderate (classical bijection, careful sum-swap). G2 moderate (the real subtlety: $\alpha$ fixed so $q^{k^\alpha}$ are genuine functions, but read as formal symbols per problem statement; must rule out accidental cancellation). G3 low (single finite computation). Overall shallow; risk is rigor about the coefficient ring (G2).

## Suggested approaches
(ii): deletion bijection or mark $(1-x^k)^{-1}=\sum_r x^{kr}$ to track $r=\mathrm{mult}_k$. (i): state Lemma C + $n=2$. Robustness: $M_v,R_v$ are $\alpha$-free integers; $M_2(2)=2\ne1$ so sides differ for every $\alpha$.

## Numerical evidence (verified)
parts = RHS for all $n\le12$; hook $\ne$ RHS for every $n\in\{2,...,12\}$. e.g. $n=2$: hook $\{1:2,2:2\}$, parts $\{1:2,2:1\}$, RHS $\{1:2,2:1\}$.

## References
Andrews, The Theory of Partitions; Bacher-Manivel, Hooks and powers of parts in partitions; Han, Nekrasov-Okounkov hook length formula. Numerical verification by brute force over partitions ($n\le12$).
